Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase. The players and the umpires are out in the middle followed by the New Zealand batters - Will Young and Devon Conway. David Willey will start with the ball. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, England have to defend a total of 311 runs to win this series. For New Zealand, the onus is on their bowlers to chase this total and level this series 2-2. Can they do it? Let's find out soon. Chase coming up shortly...

New Zealand's bowling unit performed well. They did lose Tim Southee and Benjamin Lister early on in the game due to their injuries as they couldn't complete their quota of overs. Had they got Dawid Malan's wicket a bit earlier, they would have ended up with much less total to chase. Rachin Ravindra picked up a four-fer which included the wicket of Malan as well. He was certainly the pick of the bowlers. Matt Henry and Daryl Mitchell picked up two while Kyle Jamieson has one in his kitty.

So, England ended up with 311 runs on the board. They will be slightly disappointed with their effort and they could have achieved much more than this. It was Dawid Malan's knock which was the foremost knock of their innings. He scored a blistering 127 runs. Joe Root, Jos Buttler, and Liam Livingstone chipped in with their cameos but the other batters failed to score runs. Nonetheless, this is a good total here at Lords and they have a proficient bowling unit who can well defend this total.
SIX! ENDS THE INNINGS IN STYLE! The last ball spoils the over. On middle, fuller, this is heaved over the long on fence. ENGLAND END WITH 311!

Commentary.Commentary: So we are all set for the game to begin. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Jonny Bairstow and Dawid Malan will open with their blades for England. Matt Henry will start the proceedings with the new ball. Let's play...

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Will Young, Devon Conway, Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (C)(WK), Glenn Phillips, Rachin Ravindra, Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry (In for Trent Boult), Tim Southee (In for Lockie Ferguson), Benjamin Lister.

England (Playing XI) - Jonny Bairstow, Dawid Malan, Joe Root, Harry Brook (In for Ben Stokes), Jos Buttler (C)(WK), Liam Livingstone, Moeen Ali, Sam Curran, David Willey (In for Gus Atkinson), Brydon Carse (In for Chris Woakes), Reece Topley.
TOSS - England have won the toss and will BAT first.

On the other hand, New Zealand had lost the opening two games of the T20I series but bounced back and won the remaining two to level the series. They started the ODI series on a high note by winning the first game but lost the following two and are 2-1 behind in this series. Boult has been amazing so far, and the side will look for others to perform well in this game before entering the World Cup. So, who will win? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

So, England have been trying different combinations with their side in both the batting and bowling units. Jonny Bairstow and Joe Root have been struggling with their batting so far. The skipper Jos Buttler and Livingstone look in brilliant form. The positives from their last game was the blistering 182-run knock from Ben Stokes which helped them win the last game comprehensively.

A very warm welcome folks! We have reached to the last game of this dazzling four-match ODI series of the New Zealand tour of Egland. The hosts are leading the series by 2-1 as of now and the final game will be held at the most historic venue of Lords. Earlier, the T20I series between these sides ended in a 2-2 draw. Can New Zealand level this series as well and walk out of this tour with their heads held high? Or will England win this series before coming to the mega event in India? Stay tuned to find out, as this game promises to be a cracker.
